evidence.text:
When you take the derivative of a constant number—like 5, or 10, or zero—the derivative is always zero. 

Because differentiating a constant wipes it out, going backward from a derivative means we can never be completely sure whether there was a starting constant tucked at the end of the original function. The **+ C** represents that unknown constant of integration, which stands for a family of possible antiderivatives that differ only by a vertical shift.

Let's look at how this works on the coordinate plane on your screen, which shows an x-y axis system for plotting functions. 

Suppose our derivative function is \( f(x) = 2x \) (f of x equals two x). One antiderivative is \( F(x) = x^2 \) (F of x equals x squared), but another valid antiderivative is \( x^2 + 3 \) (x squared plus three), and another is \( x^2 - 5 \) (x squared minus five).

What is the general antiderivative of \( f(x) = 3x^2 \) (f of x equals three x squared)?
A) \( x^3 + C \) (x cubed plus C)
B) \( 3x^3 + C \) (three x cubed plus C)
C) \( x^2 + C \) (x squared plus C)

evidence.text:
A secant line passes through two points on a curve, letting us calculate an average rate of change.

Here is the coordinate plane on your screen, which shows an x-y axis system for plotting functions. 

The derivative at a point is the instantaneous rate of change, defined as the limit of the average rate of change (difference quotient) as the interval shrinks to zero: \( f'(a) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(a+h) - f(a)}{h} \) (f-prime of a equals the limit as h approaches zero of f of a plus h minus f of a all divided by h). Geometrically, \( f'(a) \) (f-prime of a) is the slope of the tangent line to the curve \( y = f(x) \) (y equals f of x) at \( x = a \) (x equals a).

What happens to the slope of the secant line as the second point moves closer and closer along the curve toward the first point?
A) It approaches the slope of the tangent line at that single point
B) It becomes equal to zero because the two points merge into one
C) It becomes vertical and undefined because the distance between points disappears
